The '''2011–12 [[Super League Greece]]''' was the 76th season of the highest [[Association football|football]] league of [[Greece]] and the sixth under the name Super League. The season began in late August or early September 2011 and ended in May 2012 with the last matchday of the European play-off round. [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] were the defending champions, having won their 38th Greek championship in the [[2010–11 Super League Greece|2010–11 season]].

The league comprised 13 teams from the 2010–11 season and three promoted teams from the [[2010–11 Football League (Greece)|2010–11 Football League]].

==Teams==
[[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]], [[Panserraikos F.C.|Panserraikos]], [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis]], [[Olympiacos Volos F.C.|Olympiacos Volos]] and [[Kavala F.C.|Kavala]] were relegated at the end of the [[2010–11 Super League Greece|2010–11 season]]. AEL and Panserraikos were relegated on virtue of their league position at the end of the season; AEL had to return to the [[Football League Greece|Football League]], formerly known as ''Beta Ethniki'', after six seasons, while Panserraikos were relegated after just one season. Olympiacos Volos and Kavala were initially relegated to the [[Delta Ethniki]] due to the [[Koriopolis|ongoing match-fixing scandal]],<ref name="OLV and KAV relegated to Delta Ethniki">{{cite web | url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/olympvolou/sth-d-ethnikh-olympiakos-voloy-kai-kavala.1338610.html | title=Olympiakos Volou and Kavala to Delta Ethniki | publisher=Contra.gr | access-date=25 August 2011 | language=el | archive-date=15 April 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190415205038/https://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/olympvolou/sth-d-ethnikh-olympiakos-voloy-kai-kavala.1338610.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> but after an appeal, both teams demanded to have their cases rechecked.<ref name="Re-evaluation for OLV and KAV">{{cite web | url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/stimena/tha-eksetastoun-kai-pali-oi-fakeloi-olympiakou-voloy-kai-kavalas.1359856.html | title=Postponement until re-evaluation | publisher=Contra.gr | access-date=8 September 2011 | language=el | archive-date=30 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030040954/http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/stimena/tha-eksetastoun-kai-pali-oi-fakeloi-olympiakou-voloy-kai-kavalas.1359856.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> The Professional Sports Committee refused, however, and the original penalty stood.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/sth-d-ethnikh-olympiakos-voloy-kai-kavala.1370616.html | title=Olympiakos Volou and Kavala definitely to Delta Ethniki | publisher=Contra.gr | access-date=15 September 2011 | language=el | archive-date=30 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030041023/http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/sth-d-ethnikh-olympiakos-voloy-kai-kavala.1370616.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> On 22 October 2011, almost two months after the league had started, they were replaced by [[Doxa Drama F.C.|Doxa Drama]] and [[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/SuperLeague/sth_superleague_o_levadeiakos_kai_h_doksa_dramas.1421093.html | title=Doxa Dramas and Levadiakos to Superleague | work=Sport24 | date=22 October 2011 | access-date=22 October 2011 | language=el | archive-date=19 October 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019160908/http://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/SuperLeague/sth_superleague_o_levadeiakos_kai_h_doksa_dramas.1421093.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Iraklis were denied a licence for the 2011–12 season over unpaid debts<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18771:2011-04-20-12-07-48&catid=83:2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291|title=Αnnouncement for the teams receiving UEFA licence for the 2011–12 season (in greek)|work=Hellenic Football Federation|access-date=16 May 2011|publisher=epo.gr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426115413/http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18771:2011-04-20-12-07-48&catid=83:2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291|archive-date=26 April 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> and put into last place of the league table.<ref name="IRA relegated, AST saved">{{cite web | url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/article1086772.ece | title=Relegation for Iraklis, Asteras Tripolis saved | publisher=Contra.gr | access-date=8 September 2011|language=el}}</ref> The club was thus demoted to the [[2011–12 Football League (Greece)|2011–12 Football League]], concluding a twenty-nine-year run in the highest football league of Greece. The demotion of Iraklis eventually spared [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]] from relegation.<ref name="IRA relegated, AST saved" />

The three relegated teams have been replaced by [[2010–11 Football League (Greece)|2010–11 Football League]] champions [[Panetolikos F.C.|Panetolikos]], runners-up [[PAS Giannina F.C.|PAS Giannina]] and [[OFI Crete F.C.|OFI]] via a [[2010–11 Football League (Greece)#Promotion playoffs|play-off round]]. Panetolikos returned to the Greek top football level after 34 seasons, while PAS Giannina made their immediate comeback to the Super League.

The promotion play-off round, originally scheduled to take place in late May 2011, was postponed to late July 2011 after qualified teams OFI and [[Trikala F.C.|Trikala]] were denied a licence for the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18884:2011-05-23-11-19-57&catid=83:2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291 |title=Αnnouncement for the teams receiving UEFA licence for the 2011–12 season |language=el |work=Hellenic Football Federation |access-date=16 May 2011 |publisher=epo.gr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525174450/http://www.epo.gr/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=18884%3A2011-05-23-11-19-57&catid=83%3A2010-02-22-21-13-22&Itemid=291 |archive-date=25 May 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The decision against OFI has since been reverted after the club successfully took the case to a civil court,<ref name="OFIPromotion">{{cite web|title=OFI earns last Super League ticket|url=http://www.ekathimerini.com/4dcgi/_w_articles_wsite5_1_30/07/2011_400508|work=ekathimerini.com|publisher=[[Ekathimerini]]|access-date=1 August 2011}}</ref> enabling the side to compete in the play-offs along [[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]], [[Doxa Drama F.C.|Doxa Drama]] and [[P.A.E. G.S. Diagoras|Diagoras]]. OFI were eventually promoted as play-off winners after they were granted a walkover in their second-to-last match as their opponents Doxa Drama were not able to field a full side.<ref name="OFIPromotion" /> The [[Heraklion]] club thus returned to the Super League after two seasons.

==Play-offs==
In the play-off for Champions League, the four qualified teams play each other in a home and away [[Round-robin tournament|round robin]]. However, they do not all start with 0 points. Instead, a weighting system applies to the teams' standing at the start of the play-off mini-league. The team finishing fifth in the Super League will start the play-off with 0 points. The fifth placed team's end of season tally of points is subtracted from the sum of the points that other teams have. This number is then divided by five.

Before the last round of matches, fifth-placed club AEK Athens earned 48 points during the regular season. Based on this number and the calculations above, Panathinaikos as runners-up began the play-offs with four points ((66–48)/5 = 3.6, rounded to 4) while PAOK and Atromitos started with zero points each ((50–48)/5 = 0.4, rounded to 0).
